evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 洗: Shuowen account, readings, and cited uses
evidence.text: The entry quotes 說文: 洗 means washing the feet and is formed from 水 with 先 as phonetic (穌典切). It lists readings xiǎn and xǐ. It cites the Shiji episode 洗足, the Lunheng distinction among washing head, feet, hands, and body, a ritual-vessel washing example from the Book of Odes, and 洗 as a water vessel in the Yili. These citations identify separate uses but do not establish their precise first dates or a linear semantic chronology.
evidence.title: [A02193] 洗 - Ministry of Education 《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》

evidence.source: Fudan University Center for Unearthed Documents and Paleography
evidence.field: Article date and 洗/歬 oracle-bone analysis
evidence.text: Lei Jinbei's article, published 2012-12-27, reports Luo Zhenyu's identification of an oracle-bone graph as 洗 and Li Xiaoding's as 歬. Lei proposes that early forms represented foot washing, that graphic and sound changes yielded 歬 and 洗, and that 歬 was later borrowed for ‘go forward.’ He treats some specific graph identities as unsettled. This is a scholarly proposal rather than consensus; the opened article gives no securely established dating for the cited oracle-bone forms and its images were not visually inspected here.
evidence.title: 雷縉碚：甲骨文考釋二則

evidence.text: The entry gives two Baxter–Sagart 2014 readings for 洗: xǐ, MC sejX, OC *[s]ˤərʔ; and xiǎn, MC senX, OC *sˤərʔ. The supplied local Baxter–Sagart table also has these two 洗 rows, and 先 rows xiān / MC sen / OC *sˤər and xiàn / MC senH / OC *sˤər-s. Thus the paired local rows show an approximate onset-and-rhyme resemblance for 洗 and the first 先 reading, while the alternative 洗 reading has a different MC final in that transcription. These local rows document entries, not proof of historical sound change or phonetic role. Local provenance: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv; 洗 rows xǐ and xiǎn, 先 rows xiān and xiàn.
evidence.title: 洗 | Definition of 洗 at Definify

evidence.field: current Mandarin readings; local kMandarin rows and upstream endpoint attempts
evidence.text: The supplied local Unihan kMandarin rows give 洗 xǐ and 先 xiān (sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt, field kMandarin). Both official character-specific Unihan pages were attempted but returned internal errors, so neither page was inspected successfully and neither is cited as verified upstream content. These are current reading metadata, not evidence for an ancient sound relationship.
evidence.title: Unihan character records U+6D17 洗 and U+5148 先 (endpoints inaccessible)

evidence.field: File description, represented script style, original image link, and reuse terms
evidence.text: The exact file page identifies 先-seal.svg as a digitally created depiction of 先 in Shuowen seal-script style and links ancient-character reference databases as sources. It states that the ancient-script representation is public domain. This is a modern vector redrawing, not an artifact photograph or an attested form of 洗. Its relevance is limited to illustrating the component 先 named in the Shuowen analysis. Original file URL is https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/dd/%E5%85%88-seal.svg.

gaps: The early oracle-bone readings remain disputed; the Fudan article reports competing identifications and a later proposed relationship, but no independent reading of the glyphs was possible.
The selected glyph depicts 先 in a modern Shuowen-style redrawing; no suitable, verified 洗 historical glyph image was established in this search.

The supplied local readings permit a notation-specific comparison but do not establish that the graphic component's ancient pronunciation was identical to any particular reading of 洗. Shuowen's phonetic analysis remains a historical source assertion.
Official Unihan pages for 洗 and 先 could not be inspected because both endpoints returned internal errors. The local rows have local-file provenance only.

MOE's cited literary examples are transmitted texts. Exact manuscript dates and the development from foot washing to broader cleaning, ritual-vessel washing, the vessel sense, or figurative purification are not established here.

No phonetic-loan claim is advanced for 洗. The cited early discussion treats possible borrowing of 歬 for ‘go forward’; that proposed loan is distinct from the component 先 in 洗. No independently recoverable ancient object name is established.
No reuse terms were checked for recurring dictionary text sources. No local text extract is recommended; cited character-specific pages and concise paraphrases suffice.
